text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Press Association of Zambia said on Wednesday it would take legal action against politicians and government officials who harrassed journalists ahead of elections, which are to be held later this year.
- Miners at the Luanshya Division of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) have said they would not sign up contracts with new investors unless ZCCM paid them terminal benefits first.
- A Parliamentary committee on Wednesday accused the Zambia Privatisation Agency of rushing the sale of state-run enterprises and costing the government large sums of money in the process.

- The opposition Zambia Democratic Congress said on Wednesday it would not allow the Frederick Chiluba government to remain in office beyond October 31, when its five-year term ran out. It did not say what practical steps it would take to force the government out of office.
